canonical_definition:
Space of definitions. Across the definitions, the prevailing usage treats context utilization as how well a model incorporates available context into its output, most often retrieved documents or other externally provided information. Other definitions widen it to using the full input context rather than a small subset of tokens, or to answering from input context when that context conflicts with parametric knowledge. A smaller line of work uses related labels for effective use of prior dialog history, for combining textual context with time-series data, or for the internal storage and use of past information under the label memory utilization.

Space of facets. Papers use several near-synonymous labels, including context reliance, context usage, knowledge utilization, context integration, and memory utilization, but the scope varies. The main divide is between output-facing formulations, which ask whether retrieved or provided evidence is reflected in a response, long-context formulations, which ask whether information distributed across the input is used rather than only a small portion, and internal-mechanism formulations, which describe storing and leveraging past information. One definition also marks memory utilization as distinct from total memory capacity.

Space of measurement. In explicit linked instruments, papers link the construct to 2 measurement instruments, ConflictQA and CounterFact, both described as synthetic datasets. Beyond those links, one paper computes context utilization as a ratio between gold context items present in retrieved chunks and those matched in the response, another measures context reliance with contexts that suggest fictional answers conflicting with pretraining, and another uses Effective State-Size as a proxy for memory utilization. Papers also link it to 3 behavioral indicators, including Input regurgitation, Lost-in-the-middle, and one retrieval task, so the measurement space mixes datasets with task-specific analyses of context use.

Links. In relationship claims, it is linked to 3 constructs. One paper reports it is related to faithfulness, describing a trilemma with noise sensitivity, and separate papers relate it to Lost-in-the-middle and to one retrieval task through discussion of uneven use of lengthy inputs and overlooking the middle portion. Causal claims are more varied: one paper claims a causal relationship from context utilization to text generation quality, another from context utilization to brain alignment, and another from context utilization to input regurgitation, where data regurgitation is described as an outcome of failure to use context effectively.

definitions.text: The extent to which a generator effectively incorporates relevant information from retrieved documents into its final response.
papers: RAGChecker: A Fine-grained Framework for Diagnosing Retrieval-Augmented Generation
Radar: Fast Long-Context Decoding for Any Transformer
Reasoning Limitations of Multimodal Large Language Models. A case study of Bongard Problems

definitions.text: The degree to which a model makes use of the full available input context rather than relying on only a small portion of it.
papers: BABILong: Testing the Limits of LLMs with Long Context Reasoning-in-a-Haystack

definitions.text: The model's ability and tendency to base its answers on information provided in the input context, especially when it conflicts with pretrained knowledge.
papers: Context-Parametric Inversion: Why Instruction Finetuning May Not Actually Improve Context Reliance

definitions.text: The internal mechanism by which a model stores and leverages past information to generate future outputs, distinct from its total memory capacity.
papers: Quantifying Memory Utilization with Effective State-Size

definitions.text: The latent ability of a model to effectively incorporate and make use of externally provided information, such as retrieved documents, to perform a task.
papers: RAG-DDR: Optimizing Retrieval-Augmented Generation Using Differentiable Data Rewards

definitions.text: The latent ability of a language model to effectively leverage retrieved external information when generating responses, reflecting how well it integrates evidence into its predictions.
papers: A Reality Check on Context Utilisation for Retrieval-Augmented Generation

definitions.text: The extent to which a model incorporates and is affected by contextual information when generating text.
papers: Quantifying the Plausibility of Context Reliance in Neural Machine Translation

definitions.text: The latent ability of a model to effectively combine natural language context with numerical time series data to improve forecast accuracy and constraint satisfaction.
papers: Context is Key: A Benchmark for Forecasting with Essential Textual Information

relationships.paper: RAGChecker: A Fine-grained Framework for Diagnosing Retrieval-Augmented Generation
relationships.evidence: When tuning the generator, the trilemma of context utilization, noise sensitivity, and faithfulness makes it difficult to improve all aspects simultaneously.

neurips24: RAGChecker: A Fine-grained Framework for Diagnosing Retrieval-Augmented Generation

relationships.paper: Found in the Middle: How Language Models Use Long Contexts Better via Plug-and-Play Positional Encoding
relationships.evidence: Despite the extended context window, LLMs still face a significant challenge in long-context inference due to the uneven utilization of lengthy inputs. [15] conducted a pivotal investigation, revealing that LLMs tend to overlook the middle portion of the input. (Section 2.2)

neurips24: Found in the Middle: How Language Models Use Long Contexts Better via Plug-and-Play Positional Encoding

relationships.paper: Radar: Fast Long-Context Decoding for Any Transformer
relationships.evidence: Radar utilizes context tokens dynamically in a principled manner, resulting in significantly higher generation quality

iclr25: Radar: Fast Long-Context Decoding for Any Transformer

relationships.evidence: We compare DRUID to synthetic datasets (CounterFact, ConflictQA) and find that artificial datasets often fail to represent the complexity and diversity of realistically retrieved context (Abstract).

relationships.evidence: Our findings reveal that the initial brain alignment of models with untrained parameters is driven by context integration. (Section 1.1)
